subject: research/market-routing
professional: an online-learning / algorithmic-economics theorist reviewing for COLT, EC or ALT (the Abernethy-Chen-Vaughan cost-function-market and Herbster-Warmuth / Cesa-Bianchi tracking line); first checks: are the market = FTRL identities and the loss and regret bounds stated with the right constants, does the switching simulation reproduce, is the LMSR-vs-sparsemax comparison made at each method's own tuned learning rate, is forgetting compared with the standard tracking baseline (fixed share), and what is new against ACV 2013 and sparsemax/entmax routing

evidence.correctness: Independent numpy script run with `/usr/bin/python3.13 -I indep.py` (scratchpad/market-routing, no subject import; reads outputs dumped by subject_out.py): simplex projection on 200 random vectors matches my bisection-on-threshold projection to 8.9e-16 (1,133 exact zeros); LMSR cost equals Hanson's b*logsumexp(q/b) to 1.8e-15 and prices equal softmax to 1.1e-16; quadratic-market cost matches my own projection to 8.0e-15 and no one of 20,000 Dirichlet simplex points per case beats it (gap 0.0), so C(q) really is the max; worst-case maker loss at q=(200,0,0,0,0), n=5, b=2 is 3.218876 = b ln n for LMSR and 0.800000 = b(1-1/n)/2 for the quadratic market, matching max_loss_bound; hedge_regret_bound equals Cesa-Bianchi & Lugosi (2006) Thm 2.2 ln N/eta + eta T/8 exactly at three (n,T,b). Independent re-implementation of the switching experiment (`/usr/bin/python3.13 -I switch_indep.py`, own projection/softmax, 13 s) reproduces README:57-58 exactly (b=1: 84.4/2.6 and 75.0/1.1; b=4: 228.1/15.9 and 86.5/1.4) and the no-forgetting 374.6/372.7. Every number recomputed is right; what is wrong is the comparison drawn from them (claims, domain).
evidence.completeness: Claimed artefacts, each run: 11 tests via `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` (README:24 says '10+ tests, ~1s': Ran 11 in 0.24 s OK); `PYTHONPATH=src python3 experiments/switching.py` runs in 5.5 s (README '~6s') and reproduces the README table to one decimal; all six 'verified claims' (README:34-45) have a test that runs; the live page https://marisstella.app/research/market-routing/ returns 200 and shows '11 tests'. The companion ../decentralized-verification-markets exists. Gaps: the script prints b=0.1 and b=0.5 rows (74.3/74.1 and 76.9/74.5) that the README table drops, and those are the rows showing LMSR is as good and as sparse (1.1 active) as sparsemax at small b; the switching-regret bound and fixed-share comparison are listed as open, not done (stated).
evidence.verification: Suite green (11 tests, 0.24 s). Five mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 2 caught (forgetting disabled, routing.py:56; projection threshold > 0 -> > 0.05, simplex.py:25), 3 survived: the L2 regret bound shrunk 16x (T*n/(2b) -> T/(2b), routing.py:22) because observed regrets on iid uniform gains are 8.7-10.2 against bounds of 166.6 and 482.2, so test_regret_within_bounds cannot discriminate; the quadratic reg_range raised to 0.5 (markets.py:69), since only the LMSR bound value is pinned; and the switching comparator replaced by max(g) (routing.py:53), i.e. the metric behind every number in the experiment table has no test at all. No test pins the experiment output. ForgettingTests (tests/test_markets.py:119) is defined after `unittest.main()` (line 116), so `python3 tests/test_markets.py` runs 10, not 11, tests.
evidence.craft: Read simplex.py (27 lines), markets.py (75), routing.py (66), switching.py (49), test_markets.py (127). Small, stdlib-only, docstrings state the formulas, a clean regulariser-parameterised base class. Defects: _Market.trade (markets.py:37) zips q with dq, so a short trade silently truncates the state: `QuadraticMarket(4).trade([1.0])` returns 0.625 and leaves q=[1.0], prices [1.0], n=4 (ran it); run_routing mutates market.q directly instead of through trade; cost() recomputes price twice per trade; test_markets.py:97 is a no-op line (`g * (1.0 if i != 0 else 1.0)`); tests after the __main__ guard. A reviewer would ask for the length check before accepting.
evidence.claims: Backed and reproduced: LMSR = Hedge (test, and my softmax check), gradient/convexity, loss bounds b ln n and b(1-1/n)/2, Hedge bound, exact zeros, the README table values, '~5x' (static minimum 372.7 over b in {0.1,1,4,16,64} vs 74.1 decayed: 5.0x), 'near 373 without forgetting'. Overstated: whitepaper:15-17 (abstract) and the live page say the quadratic market 'keeps sparse, low-regret routing at liquidity values where LMSR becomes diffuse and loses accuracy'. The two markets' b are different learning-rate scales (eta=1/b on entropy vs on 1/2||p||^2), so equal-b comparison is a parameterisation confound; tuned over (b, lambda) on a 4x5 grid both reach the same regret (LMSR 74.3 +- 2.7 se, sparsemax 74.1 +- 2.5 at b=0.1, lambda=0.99) and LMSR is then as sparse (1.1 active, the script's own b=0.1 row, which the README table omits). The defensible statement is 'sparsemax is less sensitive to b', not that it routes better. Limits (one environment, 6 seeds, no CIs) are disclosed; the confound is not.
evidence.fitness: A researcher could reuse the market classes and the switching harness as a starting point. Nearest prior work: Abernethy, Chen & Vaughan 2013 (cost-function market = FTRL, the quadratic market and its b(max R - min R) loss bound are theirs), Chen & Vaughan 2010, Martins & Astudillo 2016 and Peters, Niculae & Martins 2019 (sparsemax/entmax as sparse routing), Herbster & Warmuth 1998 and Cesa-Bianchi, Gaillard, Lugosi & Stoltz 2012 (fixed share / discounted mirror descent for tracking). Props 1-3 and Obs. 4 are restatements of that work, correctly. The only new element is the decayed-market simulation, and fixed share, cited at whitepaper references but never run, matches it: my run gives 72.5 +- 2.3 at eta=1, alpha=3e-5 vs 74.1-74.3 for the tuned decayed markets. So nothing here is new and sound beyond a reproduction; the working note is not a paper-track result.
evidence.domain: Against standard online-learning practice: constants are right (CBL Thm 2.2; Orabona's FTRL corollary for the L2 case), but (a) methods are compared at a shared hyperparameter rather than each at its tuned value, (b) the tracking baseline the field uses (fixed share) is missing though cited, (c) 6 seeds with no standard errors (I measured se ~2.5 on regret ~74, so the 74.8 vs 74.2 differences in the table are noise), (d) the L2 bound uses ||g||^2 <= n; centring gains on the simplex gives ||g - c1||^2 <= n/4, a 4x tighter T n/(8b), which a reviewer would expect. A theorist would not sign off on the experimental section as written.

defects.what: The headline comparison (abstract, README reading (iii), live page) compares LMSR and the quadratic market at the same b, which is a different learning rate for each geometry; tuned per method both reach the same switching regret (74.3 +- 2.7 vs 74.1 +- 2.5) and LMSR is equally sparse (1.1 active). The sparsity 'advantage' is a parameterisation artefact, presented as a result.

Fixed share (Herbster-Warmuth), cited but never run, matches the decayed markets (72.5 +- 2.3 tuned); 'forgetting is what matters' is shown only against static routers, so the market framing's contribution over the standard tracking baseline is untested.
README table drops the b=0.1 and b=0.5 rows the script prints, which are the rows where LMSR equals sparsemax in regret and sparsity.

No test covers switching_regret or the experiment output; replacing the comparator by max(g) leaves all tests green. The L2 regret test is 16-50x slack and survives a 16x tighter bound; the quadratic reg_range is unpinned.
trade() zips q with dq, so a short bundle silently truncates the market state (QuadraticMarket(4).trade([1.0]) leaves q=[1.0], prices [1.0], n=4).
Six seeds with no standard errors in the table; my se is ~2.5 on regret ~74, so small-b differences shown are noise.
ForgettingTests is defined after `if __name__ == '__main__': unittest.main()`, so running the file directly skips it (10 of 11 tests); line 97 is a no-op transformation.
L2 regret bound uses ||g||^2 <= n; gains can be centred on the simplex (||g - c1||^2 <= n/4), giving T n/(8b), 4x tighter; 'loose' is disclosed but the standard fix is not applied.

Novelty not positioned: Props 1-3 are Abernethy-Chen-Vaughan 2013 restated, sparsemax/entmax routing (Peters-Niculae-Martins 2019) is not cited, and discounted/fixed-share tracking (Cesa-Bianchi et al. 2012) is not compared.

verdict: Small, correct, reproducible working note: every number I recomputed independently (projection, LMSR and quadratic costs, loss bounds, the Hedge constant, and the whole switching table via my own re-implementation) is right, and the 11 tests and the experiment run in seconds. It does not meet the bar. The headline finding, that the quadratic market stays sparse and low-regret where LMSR degrades, compares the two at the same b, which is a different learning rate for each; tuned per method they tie (74.3 vs 74.1, se ~2.5) and LMSR is as sparse, and the fixed-share baseline the paper cites but never runs ties too (72.5). Three of five seeded bugs survive, including one in the switching-regret metric behind every table entry. The theory is a faithful restatement of Abernethy-Chen-Vaughan 2013, so nothing here is yet new.
